text: I slipped and fell in a shopping centre in Perth. Which public liability lawyers are best?

result.keyword: I slipped and fell in a shopping centre in Perth. Which public liability lawyers are best?
result.markdown:
Yes. For a **slip-and-fall in a Perth shopping centre**, you’re generally looking at an **occupier’s liability/public liability** claim. The key issue is whether the shopping centre, retailer, or another party was negligent—for example, failing to identify or clean up a spill or otherwise leaving a foreseeable hazard. Legal Aid WA confirms that shopping centres fall within occupier’s-liability law. [www.legalaid.wa.gov.au](https://www.legalaid.wa.gov.au/node/376?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.legalaid.wa.gov.au](https://www.legalaid.wa.gov.au/find-legal-answers/managing-your-affairs/injuries/negligence?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

I wouldn’t pick a lawyer purely by Google rating, but based on **current Perth presence + specific public-liability/slip-and-fall experience**, these are the firms I’d shortlist:

| Firm | Why I'd consider them |
|---|---|
| **Stephen Browne Lawyers** | Particularly relevant: they specifically handle slip/trip/fall claims in shopping centres and say they've handled WA public-liability matters for 40+ years. Their Perth office currently has a 4.9/5 rating from 554 reviews. [www.stephenbrowne.com.au](https://www.stephenbrowne.com.au/service/public-liability/slip-trip-fall-lawyers?utm_source=chatgpt.com) |
| **LHD Lawyers Perth** | Dedicated public-liability practice, explicitly including shopping-centre injuries. Their Perth office currently has 4.9/5 from 372 reviews. [www.lhd.com.au](https://www.lhd.com.au/office-location/wa/perth/public-liability-claims/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) |
| **Turner Freeman Lawyers Perth** | Specifically lists slips/falls in shopping centres and retail properties as public-liability claims, with free initial assessments and a no-win-no-fee offering subject to conditions. [www.turnerfreeman.com.au](https://www.turnerfreeman.com.au/personal-injury-lawyers-perth/public-liability/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) |
| **Foyle Legal** | WA-focused public-liability practice that specifically discusses Perth shopping-centre slip/fall claims. Current business listing shows 4.9/5 from 297 reviews. [foylelegal.com](https://foylelegal.com/personal-injuries/public-liability-claims/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) |
| **Separovic Injury Lawyers** | Another established Perth personal-injury specialist; a current Perth legal directory lists it among the highly rated public-liability practices. [lawconnect.com](https://lawconnect.com/en-au/find/public-liability-and-claims/wa/perth-6000?utm_source=chatgpt.com) |


### My practical shortlist

If it were **my case**, I'd get **2–3 initial assessments** rather than immediately signing with the first firm. I'd start with **Stephen Browne, LHD and Turner Freeman** because their published practice information specifically matches a shopping-centre slip/fall.

Ask each lawyer:

1. **Who do you think is potentially liable—the centre, individual retailer, cleaning contractor, or someone else?**
2. **What evidence do you need from me?**
3. **Will you obtain the shopping centre's CCTV and incident report?**
4. **Is the matter genuinely no-win-no-fee, and what happens to disbursements and costs if I lose?**
5. **Are there any WA thresholds or restrictions that could affect my compensation?**
6. **Who will actually run my file—the solicitor I meet or another lawyer?**

### Do this now

If the fall was recent, **preserve evidence before anything disappears**. Legal Aid WA recommends keeping the date/time/location, witness details, photographs, medical records, expenses and correspondence. [www.legalaid.wa.gov.au](https://www.legalaid.wa.gov.au/find-legal-answers/managing-your-affairs/injuries/negligence?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

I'd also contact the shopping centre **in writing** and ask them to preserve **all CCTV footage covering the incident and surrounding area**, as well as the incident report, cleaning/inspection records and relevant maintenance records. Don't make statements accepting blame.

There are **strict time limits** for WA negligence claims, so don't leave the legal assessment until you're close to the deadline. Legal Aid WA specifically recommends obtaining advice as soon as possible. [www.legalaid.wa.gov.au](https://www.legalaid.wa.gov.au/node/376?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.legalaid.wa.gov.au](https://www.legalaid.wa.gov.au/find-legal-answers/managing-your-affairs/injuries/negligence?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

[Law Society of Western Australia — Find a Lawyer](https://www.lawsocietywa.asn.au/find-a-lawyer/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

If you tell me **which Perth shopping centre you fell in, roughly when it happened, what caused the fall (e.g. wet floor, spilled liquid, uneven surface), and what injury you suffered**, I can narrow this to **the 3 most suitable firms and compare their fees, experience and reviews**.
